reviewedEvidence.title: Waymo opens Las Vegas airport access for existing riders
reviewedEvidence.summary: Waymo says existing Las Vegas riders can use Harry Reid International Airport, with dedicated pickup zones at Terminals 1 and 3. Wider rider access will be phased.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Assess airport access as a distribution capability for GoCar: compare concession costs, pickup reliability, waiting time and contribution per trip.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Compare airport operating requirements and per-trip economics before pursuing a partnership.
reviewedEvidence.limitations: Company-reported access; no GoTo demand or unit-economic effect is established.

reviewedEvidence.title: Waymo prepares Madrid entry with a 2027 first-rider target
reviewedEvidence.summary: Waymo announced preparatory work in Madrid, beginning with manually driven vehicles and local validation. Its target is to welcome initial riders in 2027.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Use staged partner diligence for autonomous mobility: assess permits, local operations, safety validation and fleet economics before assuming commercial availability in Indonesia.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Track regulatory milestones, paid-rider availability and local operating partners separately.
reviewedEvidence.limitations: Company announcement; 2027 is a target. No Indonesian operation, licence or commercial return is established.

reviewedEvidence.title: Waymo begins Toronto preparation, targeting first riders in 2028
reviewedEvidence.summary: Waymo announced manual mapping and specialist-led testing in Toronto, with Element Fleet Management as its local fleet partner. Its goal is to welcome riders in 2028; the announcement is preparation for service, not a current driverless passenger launch.
reviewedEvidence.implication: A GoTo case study in staged autonomous-market entry, local fleet operations and validation before scale. Toronto economics and approval do not transfer automatically to Indonesia.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Map regulatory gates, fleet maintenance, validation driving and service-area economics before assessing an Indonesian partner pilot.

reviewedEvidence.title: Waymo closes USD5bn term loan to finance expansion
reviewedEvidence.summary: Waymo CFO announced a USD5bn term loan, described as its first debt financing. PIMCO, Blackstone and Sixth Street were lead syndicated lenders; Goldman Sachs was sole lead bookrunner.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Evaluate whether autonomy economics justify debt obligations before assuming platforms can finance fleets from asset-light cash flow.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Read lending terms, covenants, repayment schedule, fleet cash generation and any guarantees before comparing financing cost.
reviewedEvidence.limitations: No interest rate, covenants or maturity disclosed in the reviewed announcement; the USD5bn loan is separate from the earlier USD16bn equity financing.

reviewedEvidence.title: Waymo opens initial public rides in Las Vegas with next-generation fleet
reviewedEvidence.summary: Waymo announced initial Las Vegas public riders and said the city would join Denver and San Diego with majority Ojai fleets using its sixth-generation driver. The announced service area covered selected destinations; access would broaden gradually.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Test newer vehicle-platform economics and accessibility separately from geographic expansion headlines.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Verify service availability, vehicle economics, accessibility and remote-support needs by deployment.
reviewedEvidence.limitations: Initial service area is not citywide availability; no independently verified fleet profitability is supplied.
